views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our posture and continue the resumed talks without committing to new purchases or structural concessions, while quietly preserving our leverage (rare earths, unreliable entity list). Do not escalate — a fresh tariff or retaliation move would collapse the fragile Osaka truce and compound domestic slowdown. Press, in return, for concrete and verifiable US relief (most importantly actual easing—not just promise—of the Huawei entity-list restrictions and staying below the threatened ~$300B additional tariff tranche).

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is real but bounded, not existential. The US has List 3 at 25% on ~$250B of our exports (May 10) and has placed Huawei plus 68 affiliates on the Entity List restricting US components (May 16), directly threatening a flagship sector — consistent with the high (+0.5) firm-level anchor. Yet crushing near-term escalation has paused: at Osaka (June 29) both sides agreed to resume talks with no new tariffs 'for the time being,' though existing tariffs remain. Mitigating factors keep this from existential: China's FX reserves rose $18.23B to $3.119T in June, the yuan gained 0.6% (first monthly rise since Feb), bearish yuan bets halved, and offshore investors bought Chinese sovereign debt at a record pace on the truce — no financial-stability stress. The domestic cost is concentrated in a slowing economy (factory activity contracting, Q2 GDP set to slow further, PBOC RRR cuts expected), which argues against aggressive escalation that would deepen the slowdown. Critically, US pain is visible (10y yield fell ~2.74% to ~2.06%, Baa spreads tightened, US IP declining, Fed easing expected), supplying genuine bargaining leverage. On that basis I set threat at +0.4 (materially high, not existential) and action at +0.1 — engage, do not escalate, and extract reciprocal US concessions before any purchase commitments, which is premature while Huawei relief has not actually been delivered (a July 16 legal analysis confirms no BIS action removing Huawei yet).
key_factors: US List 3 tariffs at 25% on ~$250B of Chinese exports
Huawei and 68 affiliates on US Entity List; promised relief not yet delivered
Osaka (June 29) truce: talks resuming, no new tariffs, existing tariffs remain
China FX reserves rose to $3.119T; yuan +0.6% in June, first gain since Feb
China economy slowing (factory PMI contraction, Q2 GDP soft, RRR cuts expected)
US financial stress (10y yield ~2.06%, Baa spreads tightening, Fed easing expected) gives leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs 'for the time being.' Trump says he will ease some Huawei restrictions (Huawei remains on the Entity List; scope unclear).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
China's foreign exchange reserves rose $18.23 billion in June to $3.119 trillion... The yuan rose 0.6% against the dollar in June, marking its first monthly gain since February.
Almost two weeks after that report, we haven't seen any official action by BIS regarding removing Huawei from the Entity List...
